source.title: Rebuilding My Wardrobe with ONLY Cotton On...

tips.text: When building a wardrobe from scratch, balance categories: a few bottoms, a few tops, a layer and one pair of shoes, rather than many of one thing.
tips.why: A balanced set makes more outfits.

tips.text: Skip colours you already own several of; add pieces that expand your rotation instead.
tips.why: Duplicates add little new outfit potential.

tips.text: A matching sweatsuit only works when top and bottom are truly the same shade; near-misses look accidental.
tips.why: Slightly different tones of one colour clash.

tips.text: Avoid wearing a colour almost identical to your skin tone head to toe; it washes you out.
tips.why: You need some contrast with your skin.

tips.text: A boxy T-shirt should fall at the waist with sleeves reaching below mid-upper-arm; very short sleeves look shrunken on a boxy cut.
tips.why: Boxy proportions need length in the sleeve.

tips.text: A subtle print on the back of a tee with little or nothing on the front looks cleaner than a loud front graphic.
Plain socks without visible logos look tidier with clogs and sandals.
Baggy bootcut jeans pair naturally with boots; their flare sits over the shoe.
tips.why: The cut was made for boots.

tips.text: Think about colour before buying a layer: a brown zip-up goes with darker or bootcut jeans and a white tee more easily than with a busy graphic.
tips.why: Check new pieces against what you will wear them with.
